clue.text: Found a cartoon character in charge of some rocks

parts.note: to have found someone is to have met them
Morph is the little plasticine figure from Tony Hart's children's art programmes on British TV

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a cartoon figure placed in charge of a rock collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists class rocks altered by heat and pressure under this adjective, one of the three main rock types.

clue.text: In island resort god maintains that endless source of wine

indicators.note: the god holds or keeps the next piece within itself, so the word is wrapped round it

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war

indicators.note: the word 'that' loses its final letter, its end

parts.note: a vineyard is where grapes for wine are grown

explanation.surface: A deity on a holiday island keeps a never-ending supply of wine going.
explanation.definitionFit: This island off Massachusetts is a well-known summer holiday destination for wealthy Americans.

clue.text: End of mate, lost

indicators.note: the answer is formed of letters running across the words 'mate, lost', spanning the comma

explanation.surface: A sad farewell: the end of a friendship, a companion gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'maTE LOSt'. 'End' looks like part of 'End of mate', but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Telos is the Greek word for an ultimate aim or purpose, used in English philosophy for a final goal.

clue.text: My! Tremendous sound as birds gather to do this

definitions.text: as birds gather to do this

indicators.note: the word 'sound' in the clue tells us the two words are spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: 'my!' is an exclamation and 'tremendous' means great, so the spoken phrase is 'my great'

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the tremendous noise of a flock of birds massing before they set off.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds flocking in autumn are preparing to fly to warmer lands for the winter season.

clue.text: European work about the East

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, or around, the word 'the'

parts.note: to run a machine or business is to work it
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A description of a piece of writing or art concerned with the eastern world.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ruthene is a Ruthenian, a member of an East Slavic people of central Europe.

clue.text: Rents rise, tho' university is in trouble

indicators.note: the letter for university is placed inside the jumbled letters
letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so these words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Rents are going up, though the university is in financial difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' jumbles the letters of 'rise, tho'' and 'is in' sets the university letter inside the jumble, near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To rent something out to customers is to let them have it for a fee, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Increase conceit, working out intelligent design

indicators.note: the letters are worked out, i.e. rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Pride grows as a believer works out a theory of a designed universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligent design is a form of the religious belief that life was made by a creator, presented as a science.

clue.text: Female and male goddess joins together as this?

definitions.text: Female and male goddess joins together as this?

parts.note: her is the female object pronoun
Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love; in myth her son with Hermes fused with a nymph into one body

explanation.surface: A riddle about a deity combining both sexes in one being.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Hermaphroditus, child of Hermes and Aphrodite, became one body with the nymph Salmacis, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A being with both female and male characteristics is the very thing the clue describes, female and male joined together.

clue.text: Leader heads here having horse speed right up

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding
to speed right up is to rush more, hurrying even faster

explanation.surface: A chief makes for this spot on a horse, picking up speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader heads' are the carved heads of US presidents; the surface wants a leader heading somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Dakota mountain carved with the heads of four US presidents, national leaders, is the place meant.

clue.text: It protects two protuberances around front of pate

indicators.note: the two words go around the next letter

parts.note: ear and lug are both words for the ear, a part sticking out from the head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word 'pate' is taken

explanation.surface: A description of something guarding two bumps that sit either side of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A small plug inserted in the ear canal shields hearing from loud noise or water.

clue.text: Finish off drink at party, imbibing water in the end

indicators.note: the drinking word takes in the next letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol heavily

indicators.note: the last letter of the word 'water' is taken

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a drink at a party, finally sipping some water.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan or ship is to wreck or sink it, destroying it completely.

clue.text: It's 10 of diamonds here: schoolmates not to play

indicators.note: the letters of the short word 'to' are taken out of the larger word
letters at play are rearranged, so what remains gets jumbled

explanation.surface: A playing card, the ten of diamonds, and pupils told not to play.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 of diamonds' looks like a playing card; diamond is 10 on the mineral hardness scale. SCHOOLMATES without T and O is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral hardness scale runs from 1 for talc up to 10, where diamond sits at the top.

clue.text: Briefly smelt, holding a foul spirit

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the next letter inside it
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: something that stank smelt bad

explanation.surface: A brief whiff of something nasty containing an evil presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' takes STANK down to STAN, and 'holding' puts A inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is the archetypal evil spirit of Christian belief, and foul means wicked here.

clue.text: Put in box after end of race

definitions.meaning: to put a letter in a postbox is to send it by mail
the Latin prefix meaning after, as in postwar
the winning ... marks the finish of a horse race

explanation.surface: Someone boxed up after the finish of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: three separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mailing, the Latin prefix for later, and the finishing marker at a racecourse all share this word.

clue.text: Feminist, classy woman, to see about simple drink in Paris

indicators.note: here placing the seeing word right beside the drink, as in being about the place

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is an upper-class young woman entering society
eau is French for water, the plainest drink
voir is French for to see; 'in Paris' covers this word too

explanation.surface: A classy French woman is told to sort out a plain drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps nothing here: the French words for water and to see simply follow each other, and 'in Paris' covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Simone de Beauvoir wrote The Second Sex, a founding text of modern feminism.

clue.text: React to loud music with report to leader

indicators.note: the report piece is attached to the leader, which goes first

parts.note: a head is a leader or chief
a report is the loud noise of a gunshot or explosion

explanation.surface: A boss responds noisily to a loud performance with a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy-metal fans nod their heads violently in time with loud rock music.

clue.text: Flower, 14 pounds, made of paste?

parts.note: in crosswords a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Rhine
a stone is a British unit of weight equal to fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A flower weighing fourteen pounds, fashioned from paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is the glass used for imitation gems, and that is what this sparkly fake stone is made of.

clue.text: Was flipping struggling to get gold

indicators.note: the letters struggle out of their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete in a fury, battling for a gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' suggests losing one's temper; the definition means switching back and forth. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch that was flicked between two states was being switched back and forth, i.e. flipped.

clue.text: Raising what men produce is leading to retribution

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it to read from the bottom up

parts.note: semen is the fluid males produce

explanation.surface: Bringing up what men make leads to punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of vengeance, and her name now means deserved punishment.

clue.text: A relative not subject to improvement

parts.note: a sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member who cannot be made better.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold in their present state, with no repairs offered, are sold in this condition.

clue.text: Horror of locks?

definitions.meaning: the kind of locks meant are dreadlocks, the matted hairstyle

explanation.surface: A fear of locks, or a hairstyle that frightens.
explanation.definitionFit: Great fear is this word, and it also makes the first half of the rope-like hairstyle.

clue.text: My turn in amusing characters in European school

indicators.note: the turned word is placed inside the rearranged letters
the characters, or letters, of 'amusing' are taken and rearranged
the word 'My' is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: It is my go in a school of funny people in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' turns 'My' backwards; 'characters' rearranges the letters of 'amusing', and 'in' places the turned pair just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germany and much of central Europe this is the academic secondary school preparing pupils for university.

clue.text: Back troops into public space

parts.note: back in time means ago, as in years back
the RA, Royal Artillery, is a British army regiment

explanation.surface: Soldiers are pushed back into a public square.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek cities this was the open marketplace and gathering ground for citizens.

clue.text: Closing brief rant, back Labour

indicators.note: the word for back closes round, or encloses, the next piece

parts.note: a tail is the back end of something

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to rave is to rant wildly

explanation.surface: Wrapping up a short tirade, someone pledges support to the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party but means hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort, and also the pains of childbirth.

clue.text: One spurns singular difficulty

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
being in a corner is being in a difficult position

explanation.surface: A lone individual turns down an unusual problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who treats others with contempt and rejects them is one who spurns.

clue.text: Minor ailment troubles pass away, if drinking lots of water

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or pester them

indicators.note: the word for passing away takes in the next piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: to die is to pass away
seas are great bodies of water

explanation.surface: A minor illness worries someone into thinking they might die from drinking too much water.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang this is a mild illness such as a cold or flu, nothing serious.
